title: DSL graph view: the mesh node graph of a DSL drawn in the engine as boxes and bezier arrows, each node showing its run time
definition-of-done:
1. A scene registered in the scene list opens a DSL (a crawfish model and one fixture) and draws every statement as a rounded-rectangle box with its id, type, run time in ms and peak heap, laid out left to right by dependency depth.
2. Every NodeReference argument is drawn as a bezier arrow from the source node's output port circle to the target node's input port circle; the edge count drawn equals the NodeReference count in the parsed DSL (checked by a test).
3. Boxes are tinted by share of the total run time from a Palette, and the critical path is highlighted (dashed or thicker arrows) and named in the status line with its total ms.
4. Pan and zoom go through the existing Camera2D; text stays legible at every zoom the camera allows.
5. A new rounded-rectangle SDF drawable lives in graphics/render/sdf and reuses the existing SDF shader setup; no new classes where an existing one can hold the state.
6. Reloading the DSL (same reload path as the mesh viewer) re-runs it and updates the times without restarting the scene.
7. An ixdar-cli route returns the drawn graph as numbers (nodes with box bounds and ms, edges, critical path) so it can be verified without pixels.
8. A launch entry and a screenshot under tmp/ of a crawfish DSL's graph.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: the layout of a small hand-written DSL gives each node the depth of its longest incoming chain, and the edge list matches its NodeReference arguments.
2. Unit test: the critical path of a graph with known per-node times is the expected chain and total.
3. Run the scene on a crawfish DSL through ixdar-cli, read the graph route, check the node count, edge count and total ms against the `mesh dsl timing` route for the same run.
4. Screenshot at default zoom and zoomed in on the slowest node.
unknowns: Function calls (FunctionDef) and DSL-47's node groups: draw them collapsed as one box, or expandable to their inner nodes? Inner nodes are not timed separately today.
Function calls and DSL-47 node groups: once DSL-47 lands its node tree times inner nodes, so groups can expand; until then draw a function call as one box.
changes-made: Decided with the user 2026-10-16: a toggle available in every scene that loads a DSL, put on the shared base (ModelScene, and MeshNodeViewerScene, or what they share) rather than a separate scene. Primary use case is the quad layout scene, which needs DSL-47 (quad layout as a DSL group, scenes run through ModelScene graphs, per-node timing inside groups); DSL-47 is being finished in parallel, so build and iterate the UI first on the mesh node viewer scene, then move to the quad layout scene after DSL-47 lands. Literal arguments are listed inside the box, not drawn as ports; only referenced inputs get port circles. Tint colours: IX-25 (palettes, renamed Color constants) is not landed yet, so use existing Color constants at one site; re-point after it lands.

First working version (agent, 2026-10-16): toggle is ctrl+G on ModelScene (field graphView, a DslGraphView in ixdar.gui.ui.graph); it replaces the 3D render pass with the graph while on. DslGraphLayout (pure: nodes, NodeReference edges, longest-chain depth, barycenter crossing sweeps, critical path, box/port/text placement, lanes above columns for multi-column edges) + DslGraphView (draw, PointerRegion pan/zoom-about-cursor/click-to-focus on its own Camera2D, legible-text zoom clamp via new Camera2D.minScaleFactor/maxScaleFactor). New SDFRoundedRect + sdf_rounded_rect.fs. SDFBezier stroke width now in pixels and BezierSDF uses the full sdf_bezier.fs (the simple one NaNs on tight bends). Route GET mesh/dsl/graph (ixdar-cli mesh-dsl-graph). Hooks: ModelScene.loadGraph and the three MeshNodeViewerScene run sites call graphView.load(runtime). Crawfish IMG_4110: 75 nodes, 146 edges = 146 references, per-node ms match mesh-dsl-timing.

Revision 2: BezierSDF switched to the full sdf_bezier.fs (simple variant dropped half of tight S-curves), tint ramp BLUE_GRAY/LIGHT_NAVY/PURPLE/IXDAR by share floors 0/2/10/30%, min text 10 px, min edge 1.5 px, vector literals shown as <x, y, z>. Verified: crawfish IMG_4110 75 nodes / 146 edges = 146 references, per-node ms equal mesh-dsl-timing; reload via mesh-dsl --name fixtures/torus_layout updated the shown view to 44 nodes / 125 edges = 125 references, totals equal timing. Screenshots tmp/dsl-graph-crawfish-default.png, tmp/dsl-graph-crawfish-slowest.png (click on repaired), tmp/dsl-graph-fixture-torus-layout.png. Tests: DslGraphLayoutTest (3) pass. Left: dense fixtures need edge bundling / long-edge lanes for many fan-out edges; default framing of very wide chains shows the left end at minimum legible zoom; quad layout scene after DSL-47.

Review round 3 (2026-10-16), the user's seven items: (1) zoom out: the legible-text clamp (Camera2D min/max scale) is gone, Camera2D is master's again; the default and click-on-empty view frames the whole graph (crawfish IMG_4110: scale 0.9, whole_graph_visible true), and wheel zoom goes down to Camera2D.MIN_SCALE, a ninth of the framing. (2) Scroll bars: MenuScrollBar generalised (horizontal flag, contentLength/visibleLength/scrollOffset, press/dragTo/release, thumbStart) and used by both MenuScrollBox and the graph view, no second class; thumb length = visible share, position = pan, dragging a thumb pans, panning/zooming moves the thumbs. Measured via mesh-dsl-graph: after 12 zoom notches content 4931 px, thumb 200 of 964 px; thumb dragged 300 px -> offset 1034 -> 2569 px; panning the graph 400 px moved it back to 2169 px. MenuScrollBarTest/MenuScrollBoxWrapTest updated. (3) Small text root cause: sdf.fs anti-aliased over smoothstep(edge-fwidth, edge+fwidth) of the median, so once the atlas distance band (pxRange 10 texels of a 2048 atlas, glyphs 256 px) is under ~1 screen pixel the ramp became a binary step and thin stems and whole letters dropped out; and the font texture had only LINEAR minification, aliasing the 2048 atlas at small sizes. Fix: sdf.fs uses msdfgen's screenPxRange (ramp kept >= 1 px), fades to the MTSDF alpha channel's true distance where the band is under 2 px (mipmapped median breaks at corners), and Texture uses LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR. Before/after of the same repair_mesh box at 6/8/10/12/16 px: tmp/text-before-*px.png, tmp/text-after2-*px.png. Before, 6 and 8 px lose whole glyphs ('repaired' reads 'ra_ird'); after, every glyph is present, 10 px and up readable, 8 px borderline, 6 px (x-height ~3 px) not readable at any filter. Ink coverage inside the box (share of glyph pixels): before 0.096/0.087/0.095/0.090/0.094, after 0.107/0.094/0.100/0.103/0.100 at 6/8/10/12/16 px. Proposal, not done: below ~9 px draw each box as id + ms only at a fixed 9-10 px and drop the type, port and literal lines, rather than hiding text silently. (4) Top black bar was the view's own status-line strip (total, critical path, slowest, controls on a dark background); removed. Critical path/slowest stay as gold borders and arrows, and the numbers stay in mesh-dsl-graph (total_ms, critical_path_ms, critical_path, slowest). (5) Debug text: the status strip's text rows, plus the scene's drawSceneOverlayText (RingScene's ring numbers and error toasts) which still drew over the graph; ModelScene.drawUI now skips drawSceneOverlayText while the graph is shown. (6) ctrl+I while the graph is shown opens the same SceneModelMenu; ModelScene.controls() returns the graph view's ControlHint rows (drag pan, scroll zoom about cursor, click box focus / empty frame, scroll bars, ctrl+I menu, ctrl+G and esc back to the model). (7) Escape: closes an open ctrl+I menu first, then the graph (back to the model, no ESC menu); with the graph closed Escape does what it did. Verified: esc with menu open -> graph still shown; second esc -> shown false and the model view. Shared-change regression: SDFBezier stroke width is now in pixels, so bezier-curve-canvas's lineWidth 1 drew a hairline; set it to a named 40 px so it looks as on master. Master vs branch screenshots of the mesh-viewer ctrl+I menu and the bezier-curve-canvas code pane: glyph shapes unchanged, branch text very slightly softer (mean abs pixel diff 3.0 and 2.4 of 255 in the text regions). Screenshots: tmp/r4-graph-default.png, tmp/r4-graph-zoomed.png, tmp/r4-graph-thumb-dragged.png, tmp/r4-graph-ctrl-i.png, tmp/r4-after-escape.png, tmp/r4-model-ctrl-i.png vs tmp/master-mesh-viewer-ctrl-i.png, tmp/r4-bezier-canvas.png vs tmp/master-bezier-canvas.png, tmp/r4-text-compare-master-vs-branch.png, tmp/dsl-48-launch.png. mvn test: 499 run, 0 failures. wt done: passed, REVIEW.

Review round 5 (2026-10-17). (1) Graph view is now an EditTool. Tool hosting moved up to the shared Scene base: tools, activeTool, defaultTool, addToolSwitch(tool, hint), switchTool, refreshControls (tool switch hints, then the active tool's addControls, then the scene's setControls unless the tool replacesView), toolLabel; Scene.initGL builds controls through refreshControls. EditTool moved scenes/ring -> ixdar.scenes, with new defaults replacesView()/drawView(). OrbitTool moved to scenes/model and takes ModelScene; ModelScene's constructor makes it active and default, ModelScene.updateScene runs every tool's perFrame, Esc = close menu, else active tool's Esc, else default tool, and drawScene/drawUI draw the active tool's view and skip overlay text when it replaces the view. DslGraphView implements EditTool (name graph), registered in ModelScene.initPanes on ctrl+G, which toggles back to the default tool; its controls are listed explicitly in addControls. Removed: graphView field, shown/toggle, the view's private controls list, the ctrl+G row and graph special cases in ModelScene.escapePressed/controls(). RingScene keeps only its tool instances, registered with ctrl+R/T/J in its constructor; its switchTool/refreshControls/toolHint/toolLabel/escape overrides are gone. Checked in ring-tool scene: control rows and order as before plus ctrl+G; ctrl+R -> ring tool (its rows and Esc text 'close an unedited ring...'), Esc -> orbit, ctrl+G -> graph, Esc -> orbit. (2) Streak: sdf_line.fs took its AA width from fwidth(sigDist); distance to the axis has a kink on the axis, so a derivative quad straddling it sees symmetric values and fwidth -> 0, and smoothstep(edge+w, edge-w, d) (reversed edges, undefined in GLSL; with w=0 a division by zero) returns 0 there: transparent centre row. Fixed: w = one pixel from fwidth(scaledTextureCoord), smoothstep with ordered edges. Not reproduced headless (scanned ~80 zoom levels at 1024 and 1023 px windows); thumb AA profile identical before/after (tmp/r5-before-zoom*.png vs tmp/r5-after-zoom*.png, tmp/r5-before-strips.png, tmp/r5-after-strips.png). (3) Scroll: GLFW's x offset was dropped; now MouseTrap.scrollCallback(x, y)/queuedScrollDeltaX, PointerRegion.onScrollDelta(deltaX, deltaY), recording/replay and POST input/scroll carry deltaX (ixdar-cli scroll --deltaX). GLFW delivers no pinch, so: scroll pans both axes 30 px/unit (shift+wheel sideways), ctrl+scroll zooms by 1.15^deltaY about the cursor, clamped at Camera2D.MIN_SCALE. Measured: ctrl+scroll 4 -> scale 0.9 -> 1.574; crawfish deltaX -5 -> H offset 294 -> 444, thumb 195.8 -> 285.5; torus fixture deltaY -6/deltaX -8 -> V thumb 326.8 -> 388.3 (tmp/r5-touchpad-before-after.png). (4) ] / [ cycle the 10 slowest timed nodes (crawfish: repaired, scan, surface, ...), framing each and drawing 'hotspot k/N' above the box and in the ] controls row; while the graph tool is active the scene's own rows (mesh viewer [ ] model switch) are not in the list, so no clash (tmp/r5-hotspot-1.png, tmp/r5-hotspot-2.png, tmp/r5-graph-ctrl-i.png). mesh-dsl-graph adds active_tool, hotspots, hotspot, hotspot_rank. mvn test: 499 run, 0 failures. wt done: passed, REVIEW.

Round 6 (2026-10-17), after DSL-47 landed. Sync: conflicts only in ModelScene.loadGraph and MeshNodeViewerScene's three run sites; took master's side (executeViewerGraph, scene.graph, runSceneGraph/pull) and dropped every graphTool.load(runtime) call: the graph tool now follows ModelScene.graph itself (DslGraphView.refresh, rebuilt when the run, its root or the root's elapsedNanos changes, so a later pull that evaluates more shows up). Tool hosting in Scene, the graph tool and the scroll chain merged without conflict. DslGraphLayout now reads only the node tree: constructor (root, expandedGroups); boxes, ms and peak heap from GraphNodeContext records, literal/default/override rows from non-reference inputSources, edges from NodeReference inputSources followed through expanded groups (a parameter to the call's inputSources, a group output to outputSources); no statements, DSL text or lastTimingMs. Depth and critical path in Kahn order. Groups (DSL def or compiled NodeGroup) draw as one box with the group's total ms ('group, E expands'); E expands the box under the cursor in place, its evaluated body framed with 'path type ms  E collapses'; E on a body node or the frame collapses it; nested groups nest frames. Hotspots rank the 10 slowest leaf records of the whole tree and ] / [ open the groups around one. mesh-dsl-graph adds toggle_group, nodes[].expandable, expanded_groups. Pull evaluation: unrun nodes are not in the tree and are omitted. quad-layout bolt: collapsed model -> layout (961 ms), 2 nodes / 1 edge; expanded 11 nodes / 17 edges, field 95, seamless 188, motorcycle 29, quantize 3, embed 85, contract 79, assembly 102, relax 276, quads 72, surfaces 25 ms, all equal to mesh-dsl-timing; critical path model..surfaces 954 ms. mcg-exam bolt: only field 89, seamless 176, motorcycle 26 ms ran and are shown (4 nodes / 7 edges, group 293 ms). Crawfish IMG_4110 mesh viewer: 75 nodes / 146 edges, total 3070 ms, per-node ms equal mesh-dsl-timing; hotspot, two-axis scroll and ctrl+scroll zoom still work. ring-tool: orbit / ctrl+R ring / Esc / ctrl+G graph / Esc / ctrl+T / ctrl+J / Esc all switch as before. DslGraphLayoutTest rewritten over real runs (6 tests: diamond depths/edges, critical path, placement, expanded DSL group, nested groups, pulled compiled group). mvn test 512 run, 0 failures; tools/teavm-build.sh OK.

Round 7 (2026-10-17), the user's scroll/frame review. (1) Vertical scroll went sideways: KeyGuy set shiftMask on any Shift press and never cleared it (controlMask cleared only on LEFT_CONTROL), so after one Shift (e.g. shift+drag orbit pan) every deltaY-only scroll took DslGraphView's shift+wheel-sideways branch. Fix: keyReleased recomputes both masks from pressedKeys. Second cause found at deep zoom: the bars' pixels-per-unit was pointTransformX(1)-pointTransformX(0), two ~1e5 px floats, ~0.2% off, so each scroll jumped ~40 px sideways; now camera.width/camera.rangeX (also in draw and the route). Measured crawfish IMG_4110, scale 137.8, after a Shift tap: deltaY -3 x3 -> V offset 193.8/283.8/373.8/463.8, H offset 77931.375 unchanged; deltaX -4 -> H +120 px, V unchanged; deltaY +20 clamps at the frame top (view top 136.36 = home top 136.33). (2) Home frame = bounding box of every box and group frame padded by FRAME_MARGIN/(1-2*FRAME_MARGIN) per axis (crawfish: x -1132..21513, y -110..136). (3) Drag-pan unlimited. (4) Scroll range = home frame union the view as the last drag-pan step, zoom, focus or frame-all left it; scroll input and thumb drags move only inside it, both axes; thumb = view/range, offset = view's offset in range. So pan out -> range grows; scroll back and out again reaches the panned-to edge; drag back -> range shrinks to home union current view; F -> home. Measured, zoomed in: V content 1708 px = home height; drag 400 px out -> range top 194.1, V content 2108, thumb 578->468; scroll in 5 then out 10 -> clamped at 194.1; drag back 300 -> range top 150.8, content 1808; F -> scale 0.9, content 1024 = visible, whole_graph_visible true. At frame-all, drag right 300 -> H content 1324, thumb 746; single click empty -> no change; double-click empty -> back to home. (5) Frame-all: EditTool.frameAll() (default false = tool over the scene's view), Scene.frameAll() + Scene.emptySpaceClicked(x,y) (double-click = 2 empty clicks within 500 ms and 6 px), Scene.refreshControls adds F after the active tool's rows unless the tool binds plain F itself; ModelScene.frameAll frames the model (target mesh centre, distance frameMesh chose, angles kept) when the tool does not frame its own view. DslGraphView.frameAll frames the home frame; a click on empty space no longer frames, it only counts toward the double-click. OrbitTool takes empty clicks through a new OrbitMouseTrap.untakenClick (after the overlay strings). F with a box focused is not done. Clash: ConnectionTool binds F to repair_mesh fills, so it keeps F and gets no frame-all F; RingTool and RingRegionTool get F; double-click-empty is not bound in the three ring tools, whose single clicks are tool actions. Verified: mesh-viewer crawfish orbit F/double-click -> distance 1.5, angles kept; quad-layout bolt orbit F -> distance 1.755, target mesh centre; bolt graph expanded layout (11 nodes/17 edges), pan, F -> whole_graph_visible; ring-tool: control rows as before plus F in orbit/ring/region tools, connection F still toggles fills, ring tool F frames the model, Esc back to orbit. Route: mesh-dsl-graph adds home_frame, scroll_range, view_rect; click adds --count (2 = double-click).
